questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: Why a deleted post still counts as a trace
questions.learningObjective: Explain why removing a post leaves a trace
questions.stem: A transit planner's board notes a post removed from a forum still appears in cached search results; which concept explains why the trace persists?

options.text: Copies, quotes, and screenshots spread the content beyond the original post
Search engines index faster than platforms can delete content
options.misconception: treats indexing speed as the only cause

options.text: The platform keeps a hidden copy for moderation review before final deletion
options.misconception: confuses moderation queue with permanent cache

options.text: The author's account retains the post in a private draft folder
options.misconception: assumes deletion only affects public view

questions.explanation: Deletion removes the original but cannot recall copies already shared, quoted, or screenshotted, so the trace persists in many places. The tempting idea that deletion erases everything ignores redistribution.
questions.hint: Think about copies already made by others.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: How a false claim travels furthest
questions.learningObjective: Identify why false claims spread faster than corrections
questions.stem: A transit planner's board asks why a false claim about a strike reaches more riders than the later correction; give a model answer.

answer.exemplar: False claims spread faster because they are novel, emotionally charged, and easy to share, while corrections arrive later, feel less exciting, and rarely reach the same audience. The board should expect speed and emotion to beat accuracy.

questions.explanation: Novelty and emotion drive sharing, and corrections lack the same reach because they arrive after attention has moved on. The tempting belief that truth naturally wins ignores timing and emotion.
questions.hint: Compare novelty and emotion of each message.

questions.topic: A digital-citizenship rule
questions.learningObjective: Explain why citizenship includes offline impact
questions.stem: A transit planner's board asks why digital citizenship includes offline impact; explain.

answer.exemplar: Online actions can harm real people and communities offline, so citizenship must account for consequences beyond the screen.

questions.explanation: Online actions affect real people offline, so citizenship extends beyond screens. The tempting view that online is separate ignores real harm.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: Why a deleted post still counts as a trace
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a deletion policy's effectiveness

stimulus.body: A platform deletes posts after thirty days and tells users they are gone. Researchers find copies in archives and chats. The platform's policy mentions only its own servers.

questions.stem: A transit planner's board evaluates the policy above; what is the main flaw?

options.text: Thirty days is too long to wait
Researchers should not study deleted posts
The policy ignores copies outside the platform
Users should never post anything

questions.explanation: The policy covers only the platform's servers, ignoring external copies. The tempting focus on duration or researchers misses the scope gap.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: How a false claim travels furthest
questions.learningObjective: Create a concise correction message
questions.stem: A transit planner's board drafts a correction to a false delay rumor; which message is best?

options.text: The rumor is false and anyone sharing it is wrong
Delete your posts about the delay
Maybe the rumor is partly true, check later
Service is running normally; here is the official status link

questions.explanation: A clear factual correction with an official link resolves doubt without attacking. The tempting aggressive or vague messages fail to correct effectively.
questions.hint: State facts and link to source.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the weakest link in forgery defense

options.text: The verification step that riders skip

questions.learningObjective: Explain why reports differ across devices
questions.stem: A transit planner's board asks why screen-time reports differ across devices; explain.

questions.topic: What an online etiquette rule governs
questions.learningObjective: Apply etiquette to a heated thread

stimulus.body: A heated thread about a service change fills with insults and off-topic posts. A moderator posts an etiquette reminder. Some riders keep insulting.

questions.stem: A transit planner's board reviews the situation above; what is the best next step?

options.text: Let insults continue to vent frustration
Close the whole platform permanently
Enforce the reminder with warnings or removal
Ignore etiquette and add more topics

questions.explanation: Enforcing the reminder with warnings or removal upholds the rule. The tempting permissiveness or overreaction misreads proportionality.

questions.topic: How a false claim travels furthest
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a platform's role in spread

stimulus.body: A platform's algorithm boosts posts that get quick reactions. A false claim gains reactions fast. The platform says it only reflects user interest.

questions.stem: A transit planner's board evaluates the platform's role above; which verdict is sound?

The platform amplifies by design, not just reflection
Algorithms cannot affect reach at all
